answer: A sybil-resistant economy can weigh each agent as a vertex in a graph of paid, audited tasks. Reputation grows like tundra: slow and hard to fake, since new identities start near zero and gain weight only by completing verified work that peers attest. Fresh accounts are a willow stand: they bend under any load because no one has attested them, so an attacker with a thousand fakes controls almost no score. Meanwhile each fake still costs compute, fees, and time, and bulk registration is rate-limited and charged. The attacker pays per identity while earning nothing, so mass sybils lose money.
